newsitem.title: ITALY: PDS for gradual Stet sale if no IRI debt.
newsitem.headline: PDS for gradual Stet sale if no IRI debt.

text.p: Italy's Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) is in favour of privatisation but would prefer a more gradual sell-off for strategic firms like telecoms group Stet if state holding IRI's debts allowed it, PDS leader Massimo D'Alema was quoted as saying.

The leader of the largest party in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition was quoted in an interview to appear in financial weekly Il Mondo on Saturday. Extracts of the article were issued on Friday.

"If we hadn't been forced into a corner by the IRI crisis, perhaps a more gradual process (for Stet) could have been possible, as in other countries, because this is a sector of great strategic importance," D'Alema was quoted as saying.

"We are all for the privatisation process going forward. Naturally the privatisation of a sensitive sector like telecoms must be carried out in a manner which takes account of the interests of the nation," D'Alema said.
The sale of Stet could be delayed until late 1997 as government hopes of launching the privatisation by next March are fading fast, financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said on Friday.

Italy is under pressure to cash in on a Stet sale as soon as possible to head off a fresh crisis at its parent IRI which is heading for losses of up to three trillion lire this year and groaning under a debt burden of 22.5 trillion lire.
Under a 1993 agreement with the European Union, IRI must cut its debt to below five trillion lire.
